title: Real-world Docker Projects
subtitle: Five complete stacks you can actually run
description: Apply everything in complete, runnable projects: a Node/Postgres API, a TLS reverse proxy, a CI pipeline, a monitoring stack and a multi-stage Go service.
outcomes: Terminate TLS with a reverse proxy
Build and publish images in CI

lessons.title: Project: Node API + PostgreSQL
lessons.summary: A full-stack Compose project with health checks, migrations, secrets and a non-root image.
objectives: Compose an API with Postgres and a migration job

sections.title: The shape of the project
sections.body: The API is a small Node service with a `/health/ready` endpoint. Postgres stores data. A one-shot `migrate` service runs schema migrations and must complete before the API starts. Configuration comes from an env file; the database password is a Compose secret.

sections.code:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm npm ci

FROM deps AS build
COPY . .
RUN npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev

FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/dist ./dist
COPY --chown=node:node package.json ./
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=3s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \
  CMD node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/health/ready').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

name: acme
services:
  api:
    build: .
    image: acme/api:local
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:3000:3000"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://app:secret@db:5432/app
    secrets: [db_password]
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy }
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "healthcheck.js"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s

  migrate:
    build: .
    image: acme/api:local
    command: ["node", "dist/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://app:secret@db:5432/app
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy }
    restart: "no"

  db:
    image: postgres:16.4-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_DB: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/db_password
    secrets: [db_password]
    volumes: ["pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U app -d app"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 12

secrets:
  db_password:
    file: ./secrets/db_password.txt
volumes:
  pgdata:
sections.note: The migrate service reuses the API image. One artifact, two commands.

sections.code:
printf 'change-me' > secrets/db_password.txt
docker compose up -d --build --wait
docker compose ps
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:3000/health/ready
docker compose logs -f api
docker compose down
sections.note: `--wait` returns after services are healthy. The migration job must exit 0.

sections.title: Seed data is a separate one-shot
sections.body: Add a `seed` service under a profile and run it deliberately. Do not seed on every boot.

exercises.title: Run the stack
exercises.prompt: Create the secret file and start the project.

exercises.title: Break it
exercises.prompt: Point DATABASE_URL at the wrong host and observe the readiness failure.
exercises.expected: The API becomes unhealthy; logs show connection errors; dependent migration never completes.

options: An env var in the file

lessons.title: Project: TLS reverse proxy
lessons.summary: Caddy or nginx in front of two services, with automatic certificates and a clean network split.

sections.title: Only the proxy is public
sections.body: The proxy publishes 80/443 and joins the frontend network. The API and web app join frontend; the database joins a private backend network. Only the proxy is reachable from the internet, and the database is not reachable from the proxy.

sections.code:
name: acme
services:
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2.8-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["80:80", "443:443"]
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    networks: [frontend]
  web:
    image: acme/web:1.4
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frontend, backend]
  api:
    image: acme/api:1.4
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [frontend, backend]
  db:
    image: postgres:16.4-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [backend]
    volumes: ["pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]

networks:
  frontend:
  backend:
    internal: true
volumes:
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  pgdata:

sections.note: Caddy obtains and renews certificates automatically when the domain resolves and ports 80/443 are reachable.

sections.title: TLS is not optional in production
sections.body: Terminate TLS at the edge and forward only over private networks. If you terminate elsewhere, forward the correct scheme/headers and trust only known proxies.

exercises.title: Network split
exercises.prompt: Write networks so only caddy and web share a public network.
exercises.expected: caddy frontend; web frontend+backend; api backend; db backend.

exercises.title: Headers
exercises.prompt: Add HSTS and nosniff headers to a Caddyfile.
exercises.expected: Use the header block shown above.

questions.question: Why is the backend network internal?
questions.explain: Internal networks isolate the database tier.

lessons.title: Project: CI build and publish
lessons.summary: A GitHub Actions pipeline that builds multi-platform images with cache and push-by-digest discipline.
objectives: Build and push an image in CI
Scan and sign as a gate

sections.title: CI is a Docker client
sections.body: The runner needs the Docker CLI, Buildx and registry credentials. Use short-lived tokens, never print them, and prefer digest-pinned actions. Build multi-platform only if you actually deploy multiple architectures; it is slower.

sections.code:
name: image
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.sha }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
          provenance: true
          sbom: true
sections.note: `type=gha` uses GitHub Actions cache; `type=registry` works across CI systems.

sections.code:
# Local reproduction of the CI build
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --cache-from type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/acme/api:cache \
  --cache-to type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/acme/api:cache,mode=max \
  -t ghcr.io/acme/api:local --load .

docker scout cves ghcr.io/acme/api:local
sections.note: Reproduce CI locally before changing the workflow; it shortens the feedback loop.

sections.title: Do not build on every push to every branch
sections.body: Use path filters and concurrency cancellation. CI minutes are a finite resource and stale builds waste them.

exercises.title: Pipeline
exercises.prompt: Write the login and build-push steps for GHCR.
exercises.expected: docker/login-action with GITHUB_TOKEN and build-push-action with tags/push.

exercises.title: Cache
exercises.prompt: Add registry cache to a buildx build.

questions.question: Which cache backend is native to GitHub Actions?
questions.explain: The gha backend stores cache in Actions.

questions.question: Why use short-lived registry tokens?
questions.explain: CI credentials should be scoped and temporary.

options: How and from what the image was built

lessons.title: Project: monitoring stack
lessons.summary: A complete local observability stack with alerting rules and a dashboard you can extend.
objectives: Run Prometheus, Grafana, cAdvisor and node-exporter

sections.title: What to run
sections.body: cAdvisor for container metrics, node-exporter for host metrics, Prometheus for storage and alerting, Grafana for dashboards. Keep all ports on loopback and put authentication in front if remote access is needed.

sections.code:
name: ops-monitoring
services:
  cadvisor:
    image: gcr.io/cadvisor/cadvisor:v0.49.1
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:8080:8080"]
    volumes:
      - /:/rootfs:ro
      - /var/run:/var/run:ro
      - /sys:/sys:ro
      - /var/lib/docker/:/var/lib/docker:ro
    devices: ["/dev/kmsg"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]
  node-exporter:
    image: prom/node-exporter:v1.8.2
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:9100:9100"]
    pid: host
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v2.55.1
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:9090:9090"]
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./alerts.yml:/etc/prometheus/alerts.yml:ro
      - prometheus-data:/prometheus
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [monitoring]
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.3.0
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:3001:3000"]
    volumes: ["grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: [prometheus]
    networks: [monitoring]
networks:
  monitoring:
volumes:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-data:

# alerts.yml
groups:
  - name: containers
    rules:
      - alert: ContainerDown
        expr: up{job="cadvisor"} == 0
        for: 2m
        labels: { severity: page }
        annotations:
          summary: "cAdvisor target is down"
      - alert: HighContainerCPU
        expr: sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{container!=""}[5m])) by (name) > 0.8
        for: 10m
        labels: { severity: warning }
sections.note: Tune thresholds to your workload; a fixed 0.8 core alert is a starting point, not a universal rule.

sections.title: Do not expose cAdvisor or Prometheus publicly
sections.body: They have no authentication by default. Bind to loopback, use a private network, or put an authenticated proxy in front.

exercises.title: Deploy
exercises.prompt: Run the four-service monitoring stack locally.
exercises.expected: docker compose up -d and check all services are running.

exercises.title: Alert
exercises.prompt: Write a rule for a container restarting repeatedly.
exercises.expected: Use changes(container_start_time_seconds[10m]) or a restart counter rate.

lessons.title: Project: multi-stage Go service
lessons.summary: A static binary, a scratch runtime, non-root execution and multi-platform builds.
objectives: Build a static Go binary in a builder stage

sections.title: The smallest useful runtime
sections.body: Go can produce a fully static binary with `CGO_ENABLED=0`. A `scratch` runtime contains only the binary and CA certificates. If you need a shell for debugging, use distroless or a debug variant; do not add a shell to production for convenience.

sections.code:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM golang:1.23-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download
COPY . .
ARG TARGETOS=linux
ARG TARGETARCH=amd64
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=${TARGETOS} GOARCH=${TARGETARCH} \
    go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/server ./cmd/server

FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt /etc/ssl/certs/
COPY --from=build /out/server /server
USER 65532:65532
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/server"]
sections.note: The binary must be static. If it needs libc, use distroless/base instead of scratch.

sections.code:
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  -t ghcr.io/acme/go-service:1.0 \
  --push .

docker image inspect ghcr.io/acme/go-service:1.0 --format '{{.Size}}'
sections.note: A small image is not automatically faster at runtime, but it pulls faster and has a tiny attack surface.

sections.title: Cross-compile instead of emulating
sections.body: Set GOOS/GOARCH in the builder to produce native binaries for each platform; QEMU emulation is slower and can hide architecture-specific bugs.

exercises.title: Static build
exercises.prompt: Write the Go build RUN with static linking and stripped symbols.

exercises.title: Multi-arch
exercises.prompt: Build and push for amd64 and arm64.

questions.explain: A static binary can run in scratch.
